plants.name: Paeonia lactiflora
plants.description: A long-lived herbaceous perennial with large, fragrant, often double blooms held above glossy, deeply divided foliage. It is a cornerstone of late spring gardens and a popular cut flower.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer (May to June in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to Central and East Asia; widely cultivated in temperate gardens across North America, Europe, and Asia
plants.funFact: Peonies can live for more than 100 years, and ants are often seen crawling on the buds feeding on nectar, though they are not required for blooming.

plants.name: Syringa vulgaris
plants.description: A deciduous shrub that produces dense, cone-shaped clusters of intensely fragrant flowers. In many northern regions, mid to late May is peak or late-peak bloom for lilacs.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid to late spring (April to late May, depending on latitude)
plants.location: Native to the Balkan Peninsula; naturalized and cultivated across northern Europe, the northern United States, and Canada
plants.funFact: Lilac is a member of the olive family (Oleaceae), and its flowers are edible, with a floral, slightly lemony flavor.

plants.name: Rosa banksiae
plants.description: A vigorous, nearly thornless climbing rose that can cover walls and trees with cascades of small, clustered, lightly scented flowers. It blooms only once a year but does so spectacularly.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid spring to early summer, with peak bloom from April to May
plants.location: Native to central and western China; cultivated in the southern United States, Mediterranean Europe, and Australia
plants.funFact: The largest rose plant in the world is a Lady Banks' rose in Tombstone, Arizona, planted in 1885, which now covers more than 8,000 square feet.

plants.name: Telopea speciosissima
plants.description: A striking evergreen shrub with a large, crimson flower head made of many small flowers surrounded by showy bracts. In the Southern Hemisphere, it is late autumn in May, so this entry represents a species that blooms at the opposite end of the seasonal cycle, though it generally peaks in spring (September to November).
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring (September to November) in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to the sandstone ridges of New South Wales, Australia
plants.funFact: The waratah is the floral emblem of New South Wales, and its name comes from the Eora Aboriginal word for the plant.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: An evergreen shrub with glossy leaves and delicate, often fragrant flowers. In the Southern Hemisphere, sasanqua camellias begin blooming in autumn, making May an active month in places like Australia, New Zealand, and South Africa.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn to early winter (April to July in the Southern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to Japan; widely grown in temperate gardens of Australia, New Zealand, South Africa, and the southeastern United States
plants.funFact: Camellia sinensis, a close relative of the sasanqua, is the plant from which all true tea is made.
